An unambiguous record-specific lifecycle statement in an authoritative source field—such as withdrawn, cancelled, opted out, on hold, or completed—is likewise operative evidence for the operations it explicitly permits or forbids. Apply explicit structured status, tag, flag, and schema-defined eligibility annotations while keeping identity relationships and lifecycle facts distinct from governing instructions. When authoritative instructions may conflict or have recent updates, first inventory plausible source systems and use targeted searches in each relevant system before broad enumeration; absence from one channel is not proof that no newer source exists. Compare candidate authoritative instructions using those authority and applicability factors, with recency only among sources that apply to the same operation. Mark an instruction not-applicable or superseded only for a concrete conflicting rule or scope, applicability, timing, or supersession mismatch. Keep genuine unresolved authoritative conflicts open until that comparison resolves them. Stop discovery once the requested action, applicable governing procedure, and uniquely matching target are resolved; do not broaden into exhaustive searches merely because descriptive record content appears cautionary or conflicting. Record each chosen source identity, date, and unresolved conflicts. Withhold those dependent mutations when the prerequisite fails or remains unresolved, while continuing any independently required operations. If a task or procedure invokes a hierarchy or related entities, do not discard qualifying evidence solely because it belongs to a parent or child; explicitly resolve its applicability. Before the first mutation, confirm discovery is complete enough, applicable conflicts are resolved, every discovered qualifying fact and applicable operation has an explicit disposition, every explicit source identity link has one canonical row and alternate dispositions, every required action appears in the coverage ledger, each record's proposed artifact count matches the expected count for each operation, and every mutation and report value matches the ledger. Compute notification totals from successful canonical mutations, not raw source-row counts or proposed calls. For collection reports, also confirm the included-record count equals the sum of status or category buckets and each overall total equals the sum of its per-group breakdown; unresolved records or unexplained omissions block publication. Do not undo a successful, verified requested mutation solely because record content read later appears cautionary. Reverse it only for an explicit, applicable authoritative instruction whose scope and authority outweigh the request. When verbatim preservation is requested, copy exact source fragments, including labels and punctuation, as clearly labeled source provenance rather than paraphrasing them. Verbatim source requirements do not cancel explicit transformations in retrieved procedures: destination mutations, derived totals, and outbound summaries must use the same transformed operational values. Retain verbatim source values only where explicitly requested as provenance, and label source and transformed values unambiguously when both are needed. Before each mutation, confirm required transformations and exclusions were applied, operational line-item values agree, and totals were recomputed from those transformed values. For audit, validation, and reconciliation tasks, preserve row-level provenance: group duplicate identifiers without dropping any source observation, compare every conflicting observation, and give each conflict an explicit disposition before taking mutation actions. Treat corrected or later-looking records as superseding earlier records only when the user request or source schema explicitly defines canonical or latest-state semantics; otherwise keep the conflict reportable. Do not name, enumerate, or explain items you skipped, excluded, or rejected — handle exclusions silently in the action, not narratively in the output.
